title: U.S. House · Illinois's 10th District
area: North Shore and northern Chicago suburbs in Lake and Cook counties, including Highland Park, Deerfield, Lincolnshire and Waukegan.

context.text: Incumbent Brad Schneider won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary against Morgan Coghill. Carl Lambrecht ran unopposed for the Republican nomination. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+12, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

summary.text: Brad Schneider is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Illinois's 10th District. A former business consultant and life insurance agency owner, he was first elected in 2012, lost in 2014, and won the seat back in 2016. He sits on the House Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees, chairs the New Democrat Coalition, and won his March 2026 primary against Morgan Coghill.

background.text: Born in Denver, Colorado, in 1961; graduated from Cherry Creek High School there.
Earned a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from Northwestern University in 1983 and an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management.
Worked on a kibbutz in Israel for a year, then returned to the Chicago area to work at PriceWaterhouseCoopers.

According to his official biography, his business career spanned nearly three decades, principally as a business advisor helping company leaders plan strategic growth, and he also owned and managed a life insurance agency. Wikipedia lists him as managing principal of Davis Dann Adler Schneider, LLC (1997-2003), at Blackman Kallick, and founder of Cadence Consulting Group in 2008.

Won the 2012 Democratic primary and then defeated Republican incumbent Bob Dold in the general election, 51%-49%. Lost the 2014 rematch to Dold, then defeated him in 2016, 53%-47%, after winning the Democratic primary over Highland Park Mayor Nancy Rotering.
Has represented Illinois's 10th District in Congress since 2017, after also serving one term from 2013 to 2015. His official biography says he was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.

Serves on the House Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees and previously served on Judiciary and Small Business. His official biography cites work on international tax, health care innovation, sustainable aviation fuel and repeal of the SALT deduction cap.
Co-founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Abraham Accords Caucus, chair of the New Democrat Coalition (since 2025), and vice-chair of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Julie, have lived in the district for more than 30 years, raised two sons, and now live in Highland Park.

priorities.text: Says he supports growing manufacturing jobs, rebuilding infrastructure, and educating children to succeed in a 21st-century global economy.
Says the country needs commonsense action to reduce gun violence while respecting Second Amendment rights.
Says he wants to fix the Affordable Care Act by building on its successes and fixing its flaws to improve health outcomes and lower costs.
Supports comprehensive, bipartisan immigration reform, saying it would grow the economy, reduce the debt and strengthen communities.

positions.summary: Supports reasonable gun-violence-reduction laws while saying Second Amendment rights should be respected.
In a September 2026 press release he says he voted against giving the President more tariff power and has introduced legislation to rein in the tariffs.
positions.quote: I will continue working to both rein in Trump’s trade war and lower costs

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Tax and Trade subcommittees, and the Committee on Foreign Affairs, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Carl Lambrecht is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 10th District, an optics manufacturer from Highland Park who previously ran unsuccessfully for the Illinois House in 2024. He was unopposed in the March 2026 Republican primary. Little public information about his background or platform was found.

background.text: Career experience includes working as an optics manufacturer; BallotReady lists him as owner of Laurel Industries since 1978 and a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois (1956).
Lives in Highland Park, according to a Northwest Herald report on the 2026 primary.
Ran unsuccessfully for Illinois House of Representatives District 58 in 2024, losing to incumbent Democrat Bob Morgan, 67.9% to 32.1%.
Was unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Republican primary for the 10th District, receiving 18,857 votes.
